interactions.flavorLineOne:
"The Loom requires material input to function; strands of basic matter that can be repurposed as needed," Ada explains.

"I've used the BrayTech schematics to create smaller devices called Threaders—with these, you can convert Glimmer into the Synthcord that the Loom needs. We should verify the Threaders are functioning before anything else…"

Purchase an Armor Synthesis bounty from Ada.

"I don't think there's much else for me to review with you. Please keep utilizing the Loom so I can compile more data—who knows where it will lead. And thank you again, Guardian."

She turns back to her workstation but stops abruptly, turning her attention back to you.

"What is it that old saying? The ball is in your court now?"

She tilts her head.

"I'm not really sure what that means—but good luck, friend."

Ada looks up from her work as you approach.

"I've been doing some experiments with the Sieve. Customized reinforcements for our veteran Guardians."

She gestures to some neatly stacked boxes, which light the room with an enticing yellow glow. 

"I discovered a method to reproduce some of our most effective armor. It worked wonderfully but proved too expensive for mass production."

"It would be a waste to let the prototypes go unused, so the Vanguard authorized me to distribute them." She hands you a small pile of requisition orders.

"Just remember—I only have so many to hand out. Once you've made your selections, let me know, and I'll pull them out of storage for you."
Ada is awestruck at what she has accomplished with the Loom, and relieved to have a new beginning for the Armory. She thanks you for your help and expresses excitement about the future.
Ada-1 examines the gift skeptically. Eventually, she looks up and thanks you, but she still seems perplexed by the exchange.

"Here it is—the first printing," Ada says tenuously.

"This is Synthweave, a programmable matter more sophisticated than I've ever seen, significantly more advanced than Glimmer."

She hands you a sample of the Loom's output.

"Do the honors of trying it out. It should be able to replicate the physical appearance of some of your armor, though not the material or energy properties."

Use Synthweave to create an ornament from your collection of Legendary armor.

Ada tells you that the Black Armory Forges have been lost. In their absence, she is working on a new project; some unfinished research she unearthed in the BrayTech archives on Europa.

She says she needs help retrieving the last remaining research data from Europa's surface, as it's not accessible via the network.

Travel to the BrayTech facility on Europa and recover the data.

"Good," Ada says as she types feverishly on her workstation.

"I used the data you streamed from Europa to make some final adjustments to the device.

"The original plans from Clovis are out of reach — whatever he wanted to make from this, it requires theoretical alloys that don't exist. Given what we know about him now, maybe it's best if that vision never comes to fruition…

"In any case, I was able to use some concepts from the original Forge designs to finish the prototype. It's my own design now.

She steps back from the workstation.

"The processing unit is the final piece. You retrieved it, it's only fair that you get to close this out."

Interact with the Loom prototype to connect the processing unit.

Ada admires your newly minted Synthweave as you approach.

"I must admit, it was a little unnerving to watch someone else operate the Loom. I've put quite a lot of effort into creating this and… I'm feeling a bit protective."

She clears her throat and fixes her posture.

"That being said, it clearly worked as intended. I've gathered data from your production job—with enough information, I may be able to amend this technology toward some other purpose in the future."

"To that end, let's start another production run."

 Acquire Glimmer in order to purchase another Armor Synthesis bounty from Ada-1.

Ada's mechanical fingers clack away at a glass touchscreen. "Initial readouts look promising—power levels are stable and the operating system hasn't hit any assertions."

She says the words carefully and meticulously, like they don't fit well around her voice yet.

"As far as I can tell, the Loom is ready for production. Let me give it a test run and see what we get, and if it passes quality checks, I'll explain the process."
